The invention relates to a transportation system designed for moving large items, such as flanges and similar heavy or bulky components. The system provides a stable and practical structure for supporting such items during transport, while also allowing efficient handling and secure placement during shipping.

The transportation system includes a frame that extends in three directions: a longitudinal direction, a transversal direction, and a vertical direction. This three-dimensional frame structure provides the necessary strength and rigidity for carrying large items and maintaining their position during transport.

The frame comprises two longitudinal girders that extend along the length of the system. These longitudinal girders are connected to multiple pairs of transversal primary support beams. The transversal primary support beams extend across the width of the frame and are arranged in pairs at spaced intervals along the longitudinal direction. Together, the longitudinal girders and the transversal primary support beams form a robust support structure.

A storage area is defined between two transversal primary support beams. This storage area is intended to receive and hold a large item, such as a flange. The arrangement of the support beams provides free downward access to the storage area, meaning that the large item can extend downwardly between the beams without obstruction. This is particularly useful for transporting items that are too large or irregularly shaped to rest entirely on a flat surface.

The lower part of the frame is configured with dimensions and locking mechanisms corresponding to those of a standard freight container. As a result, the transportation system can be positioned on top of a freight container and safely secured in place. This compatibility allows the system to be integrated into existing freight transport infrastructure, improving handling efficiency and ensuring safe transport of large items.
outputs.L4:
The transportation system is designed for carrying large, heavy, or bulky items, such as flanges, rings, structural components, or similar industrial goods. It comprises a stable frame structure having longitudinal girders and transverse support beams. These beams are arranged so that they define one or more storage areas in which the items to be transported can be received and supported. The storage areas are accessible from below, allowing lifting equipment, handling tools, or securing devices to engage the transported items from the underside. This configuration facilitates loading, unloading, and safe positioning of the goods within the frame.

The frame is constructed to withstand the forces that occur during handling and transport. The longitudinal girders provide the main load-bearing structure, while the transverse support beams distribute the weight of the stored items and help maintain the rigidity of the system. The arrangement of the support beams may be adapted to the shape and size of the goods being carried, so that large items can be held securely without excessive movement. In particular, the system is suitable for transporting flanges or comparable components that require reliable support and protection during shipment.

A key feature of the transportation system is that it includes a lower frame configured to be compatible with a standard freight container. The lower frame is dimensioned and arranged so that it can be placed on top of a freight container in a secure and stable manner. It is provided with locking mechanisms that correspond to the container’s standard securing points, such as corner fittings or twist-lock connections. These locking mechanisms allow the transportation system to be mechanically fixed to the freight container, preventing displacement, tipping, or accidental separation during transport.

Because of this freight-container-compatible design, the transportation system can be integrated into existing logistics chains without requiring special transport platforms or custom securing arrangements. The system may be lifted, stacked, transported, and secured using conventional container-handling equipment. When mounted on a freight container, the lower frame distributes loads appropriately and ensures that the transported items remain safely positioned above the container during road, rail, sea, or intermodal transport.

Overall, the transportation system provides a robust and practical solution for shipping large industrial items. By combining a load-bearing frame with defined storage areas and a container-compatible locking frame, it enables safe handling, secure transport, and efficient integration with standard freight-container logistics.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may seem small and ordinary, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, and its purpose is to point to something specific. When we say “a book,” we might mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener already know about.

“The” helps give clarity and direction to a sentence. It can refer to people, places, objects, ideas, or experiences. For example, “the sun,” “the city,” “the answer,” and “the moment” all feel specific and meaningful because of this tiny word.

Although it is only three letters long, “the” appears everywhere in English. It connects thoughts, organizes meaning, and makes communication more precise. Without it, many sentences would feel incomplete or unclear. In a way, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a big impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract/claim description for a transportation system for large flanges, including a frame with longitudinal girders, transverse support beams, storage areas with downward access, and container-compatible locking mechanisms.
counterfactuals.output:
## Abstract

A transportation system for large flanges is provided, in particular for transporting annular or ring-shaped flanges used in wind turbines, industrial plants, pipelines, offshore structures, or similar large-scale installations. The system comprises a load-bearing frame having at least two longitudinal girders extending in a transport direction and a plurality of transverse support beams connected between the longitudinal girders. The longitudinal girders and transverse support beams define one or more storage areas configured to receive one or more large flanges in a substantially horizontal or inclined orientation. At least one storage area is open or accessible from below so that a flange can be inserted into, supported in, or removed from the frame by lifting equipment approaching from a lower side of the frame. The frame further comprises locking mechanisms arranged at standardized container interface positions, such as corner castings, twist-lock fittings, or ISO-container-compatible coupling points, enabling the transportation system to be secured to a truck chassis, rail wagon, vessel deck, container stack, or handling device. The system thereby permits safe and efficient multimodal transport, storage, lifting, and handling of large flanges while maintaining compatibility with existing container logistics infrastructure.

## Exemplary Claim Description

1. **A transportation system for large flanges**, comprising:  
   a load-bearing frame having a first longitudinal girder and a second longitudinal girder extending substantially parallel to one another in a longitudinal transport direction;  
   a plurality of transverse support beams extending between and connected to the first and second longitudinal girders;  
   at least one flange storage area defined at least in part by the longitudinal girders and the transverse support beams, the flange storage area being configured to receive and support at least one large flange; and  
   a plurality of locking mechanisms arranged on the frame, the locking mechanisms being configured for engagement with standardized container securing devices.

2. **The transportation system of claim 1**, wherein the at least one flange storage area comprises a downwardly accessible receiving region configured to permit insertion or removal of the large flange from a lower side of the frame.

3. **The transportation system of claim 1 or 2**, wherein the transverse support beams are spaced apart along the longitudinal transport direction to define a plurality of flange storage areas.

4. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein each flange storage area is configured to receive a flange having a central opening, and wherein at least one support surface is positioned to engage an annular portion of the flange.

5. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the frame comprises support seats, brackets, pads, or saddles arranged on the transverse support beams for supporting the flange at a plurality of circumferentially spaced support points.

6. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the downwardly accessible receiving region is located between adjacent transverse support beams and between the first and second longitudinal girders.

7. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the locking mechanisms comprise twist-lock-compatible corner fittings arranged at positions corresponding to standardized ISO container corner positions.

8. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the locking mechanisms are configured to secure the transportation system to at least one of a container chassis, a rail wagon, a ship deck, a storage rack, or another transportation system.

9. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the longitudinal girders define outer side members of the frame and provide primary bending resistance during lifting and transport.

10. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, further comprising lifting interfaces configured to be engaged by a crane, spreader, forklift, or straddle carrier.

11. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the frame has external dimensions corresponding substantially to an ISO freight container footprint.

12. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, further comprising retaining elements configured to prevent lateral, vertical, or longitudinal displacement of the flange during transport.

13. **The transportation system of claim 12**, wherein the retaining elements comprise adjustable clamps, bolted retaining arms, locking pins, straps, wedges, or removable stop members.

14. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the transverse support beams are removably or adjustably connected to the longitudinal girders to accommodate flanges of different diameters or thicknesses.

15. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the at least one flange storage area is configured so that a flange can be lifted into the storage area from beneath the frame while the transportation system is positioned on a support structure having clearance below the frame.

16. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the frame includes at least one lower opening aligned with the flange storage area to provide access for lifting forks, slings, hooks, or a lifting platform.

17. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the storage area is configured to store the flange below an upper plane of the frame, thereby reducing the overall transport height.

18. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the frame is stackable with another identical transportation system by means of the container-compatible locking mechanisms.

19. **The transportation system of any preceding claim**, wherein the longitudinal girders and transverse support beams are formed of steel box sections, I-beams, channel sections, tubular sections, or welded plate structures.

20. **A method of transporting a large flange**, comprising:  
   positioning a transportation system according to any of claims 1 to 19 above a lifting region;  
   moving a large flange upwardly into a downwardly accessible flange storage area of the frame;  
   supporting the large flange on one or more transverse support beams or support seats;  
   securing the large flange against displacement; and  
   locking the transportation system to a transport vehicle or storage structure using container-compatible locking mechanisms.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical invention disclosure paragraph using reference numerals for a frame-based transport rack that can be locked on top of a freight container and used to carry large items such as flanges.
counterfactuals.output: A frame-based transport rack (100) is disclosed for removably securing large, heavy, or irregular cargo items, such as pipe flanges (10), on an upper surface of a freight container (20). The transport rack (100) includes a rigid base frame (102) formed from longitudinal beams (104) and transverse beams (106) defining a load-supporting platform sized to span at least a portion of the freight container roof (22). Corner locking assemblies (110) are mounted at or near respective corners of the base frame (102) and are configured to engage corresponding upper corner castings (24) of the freight container (20), such as by twist-lock members (112), latch pins, or equivalent container-locking mechanisms, thereby releasably locking the rack (100) to the container (20) during transport. One or more cargo support cradles (120), upright posts (122), retaining brackets (124), and adjustable tie-down points (126) are coupled to the base frame (102) to receive and restrain the flanges (10) in a stable orientation, with optional spacer pads (128) or saddles configured to distribute load and reduce localized stress. The rack (100) may further include lifting lugs (130) for crane handling, forklift pockets (132) for ground handling, and removable or adjustable crossmembers (134) to accommodate flange sizes of different diameters and thicknesses. In use, the rack (100) is positioned on the freight container (20), the locking assemblies (110) are engaged with the upper corner castings (24), and the flanges (10) are secured to the support cradles (120) using chains, straps, clamps, or other retainers (140), thereby enabling large cargo items to be transported on top of the container (20) without requiring modification of the container structure.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a formal patent specification excerpt beginning “The invention relates to a transportation system…” for transporting large circular industrial components, with X/Y/Z frame directions, upper support beams, downward free access, and container twist-lock compatibility.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention relates to a transportation system for transporting large circular industrial components, in particular annular, cylindrical, or substantially disk-shaped components such as tower sections, nacelle parts, rotor hubs, bearings, flanges, rings, pressure-vessel sections, or wind-turbine components, wherein the transportation system comprises a load-supporting frame defining mutually orthogonal frame directions X, Y and Z.

In one embodiment, the X direction corresponds to a longitudinal direction of the frame, the Y direction corresponds to a transverse direction of the frame, and the Z direction corresponds to a vertical direction of the frame when the transportation system is arranged in an operative transport position. The frame comprises a lower frame structure and an upper frame structure, the upper frame structure including at least two upper support beams extending substantially in the X direction and being spaced apart in the Y direction. The upper support beams are configured to support or laterally retain a large circular industrial component received between or upon the upper support beams.

The transportation system is configured such that, when the circular industrial component is mounted to the frame, a lower region beneath the component remains at least partially open in the Z direction, thereby providing downward free access to the component and/or to fastening, lifting, securing, inspection, or service regions associated with the component. The downward free access may be provided by an absence of cross-members directly below a central portion of the component, by a recessed lower frame geometry, or by positioning load-bearing members laterally outside a downward access zone.

In a further embodiment, the frame comprises a plurality of corner fittings arranged at standardized container interface positions. The corner fittings are configured for cooperation with container twist-lock devices, such that the transportation system is compatible with conventional container handling equipment, including twist-lock securing devices on road trailers, rail wagons, sea-going vessels, handling frames, spreaders, or storage platforms. The corner fittings may be arranged in accordance with ISO container spacing, thereby enabling the transportation system to be secured, lifted, stacked, or handled using existing intermodal transport infrastructure.

The upper support beams may be provided with support interfaces, saddles, brackets, adjustable contact members, or replaceable pads adapted to engage an outer circumferential surface, an inner circumferential surface, or end-face regions of the circular industrial component. The support interfaces may be adjustable in at least one of the X, Y, and Z directions to accommodate components of different diameters, widths, or mass distributions. In particular, the support interfaces may define a receiving space having a curved or polygonal support contour corresponding generally to the circular geometry of the component.

The frame may further comprise transverse connecting members extending in the Y direction between longitudinal frame members, vertical or inclined struts extending generally in the Z direction, and reinforcement elements arranged to transfer loads from the upper support beams to the container-compatible corner fittings. The load path from the component to the corner fittings may thereby be established while preserving the downward free access below the component.

In use, a large circular industrial component is positioned relative to the frame such that a central axis of the component extends substantially in the X direction, substantially in the Y direction, or substantially in the Z direction, depending on the intended transport configuration. The component is then supported by the upper support beams and secured by fastening devices, clamps, straps, pins, bolted connections, or other releasable securing elements. Once secured, the transportation system may be fixed to a transport platform by engagement of twist-lock devices with the corner fittings.

Accordingly, the transportation system enables secure transport of large circular industrial components while maintaining compatibility with standardized container logistics and while providing downward free access for handling, inspection, assembly, or removal operations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
